title: Experiment configuration
description: One file in configs/benchmarks/ - the declarative "what to measure", kept strictly separate from configs/models.yaml's "which candidate" (docs/note.md §8). An experiment names a candidate set and a grid of workload points; expanding the grid produces one benchmark_result document per cell. Deliberately expresses grids rather than single points, because docs/note.md §11/§12's context- and output-length sweeps are the core experiments and a config format that can only express one point forces the sweep back into CLI flags - which docs/TODO.md GATE 3 explicitly forbids ("no CLI flags carrying experimental meaning"). Self-contained (no cross-file $ref) so validation needs no resolver.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema the file targets. Bumped when the config format changes shape; results record the version they were produced under so an old campaign stays interpretable.

name.description: Stable identifier, and a component of every experiment_id this config generates. Renaming it orphans the results that reference it, so treat it as append-only in the same way registry rows are.

description.description: Required, and required to state the hypothesis. docs/note.md §57: every experiment answers "what hypothesis does this test, what variable changed, what was held constant, what is expected to move". A config without that sentence is a script, not an experiment.

tier.description: docs/note.md §18. smoke = 10-50 samples, catches broken serving/tokenizer/chat-template/quantization; regression = small but representative, run for every candidate; full = final candidates only; holdout = never used for tuning, final evaluation only. Mostly a sample-count and cost signal, but recorded so a headline number can never be quietly a smoke run.

models.description: Keys into configs/models.yaml. Keys, never inline model definitions: the registry stays the single place a candidate is described, so two experiments can never disagree about what `7b-awq-vllm-orin` means.

workload.description: The swept grid. Every array here is a full axis: the runner takes the Cartesian product of these lists, so a two-element list doubles the campaign. docs/note.md §4 warns against the full product - keep one or two axes open per experiment and pin the rest.

input_tokens.description: Target prompt lengths in TOKENS, not characters - the prompt must be built to hit these, and the achieved count recorded from the server's own `usage`, because a target and an achieved token count are not the same number. Canonical ladder (docs/note.md §11): 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384. Values above a candidate's max_model_len/ctx_size are an error, not a silent truncation.

output_tokens.description: max_tokens per request (docs/note.md §12: 32/128/256/512...). Separating this axis from input_tokens is what stops a model looking fast merely because it generates less. The 16/32/64/128/256/512 ladder is also embedded-ai-chain/docs/paper.md's P3 core experiment verbatim.

batch_size.description: Requests submitted together in one batch. NOT interchangeable with concurrency - docs/note.md §13 forbids mixing the terms, since they are different experimental conditions that happen to produce similar throughput curves.

concurrency.description: Independent in-flight requests. batch=1/concurrency=1 is the deployment reality for embedded-ai-chain; everything above it is characterisation and must be labelled as such.

prompt_source.description: How the prompt of a given token length is constructed. Must be deterministic and versioned - a prompt that varies between runs makes prefill timings incomparable.

prompt_template_version.description: docs/note.md §21. Bumped whenever the system prompt, user template, or tool schema changes. A template change is an experimental change and must be visible in the results, not hidden in the implementation.

tools.description: Tool schema set attached to each request, or null for none. Performance runs normally attach none; tool-calling behaviour is measured separately (see quality_result.schema.json). Recorded either way, because attaching tools changes prompt length and can change the decode path.

sampling.description: Pinned explicitly, never inherited from the server. This lab has already measured that server defaults change behaviour and not just wording: at llama.cpp's default (~0.8) Qwen2.5-1.5B emits a correct tool call 12/15 times; at 0.1 it is 15/15.

temperature.description: 0.0 for performance benchmarking. Note that vLLM and llama.cpp do not both treat 0.0 identically in every build - if a run needs a nonzero floor, say so in `description` rather than changing it silently for one backend (docs/note.md §41).

seed.description: Fixed seed where the backend honours one. null means the backend does not support it - record that rather than pretending the run was deterministic.

repetitions.description: Warmup and measurement policy. These are FLOORS, not the policy itself: benchmarks/harness.py warms up until junction temperature is flat across a rolling window and records warmup_reached_steady_state=false when it gives up. docs/note.md §4's fixed "warmup: 5" would be a regression against that and is deliberately not adopted.

warmup_min.description: Minimum warmup iterations before steady-state detection is even consulted.

warmup_max.description: Cap after which warmup stops regardless, with warmup_reached_steady_state=false recorded.

measurement_runs.description: Minimum measured repetitions per cell. >=30 for a publication cell (docs/note.md §48); raise it where variance is high rather than reporting a tighter interval than the data supports.

min_measurement_s.description: Wall-clock floor for the measurement window. Exists because tegrastats samples at 500ms: a cell that finishes its runs in under a couple of seconds yields too few power samples for a meaningful energy figure, regardless of how many repetitions it did.

outlier_policy.description: docs/note.md §10. Default and strong preference is `none`: raw runs are all preserved and percentiles are computed over everything. `flag-only` annotates suspected outliers without dropping them. Silent discarding is not an option in this enum on purpose.

execution_condition.description: docs/note.md §15, and the field that makes the whole co-residency study possible. standalone = only the LLM workload is active. co-resident = the real embedded-ai-chain pipeline is running alongside. No default is permitted anywhere in this repo: on a unified-memory board an unlabelled number is uninterpretable, and every published figure must say which condition it came from.

co_resident_workload.description: Required in spirit whenever execution_condition is co-resident: which components were actually running (yolo, stt, tts, vlm), so the condition is reproducible rather than a vague "under load".

platform_state.description: The hardware performance state the campaign requires. docs/note.md §39's protocol sets these BEFORE the run; the result records what was actually observed, and the two are compared. A mismatch invalidates the cell rather than being averaged in.

nvpmodel_mode.description: Required power mode, e.g. "MAXN" / "0". docs/note.md §27: do not assume Orin's modes transfer to Thor.

jetson_clocks.description: Whether clocks must be pinned. Verified via the min==max sysfs heuristic in benchmarks/harness.py - two weaker checks were tried and both gave wrong answers live on this device.

require_reboot.description: docs/note.md §39 step 1. Rarely needed; recorded when it is.

notes.description: Free text. Known confounds belong here and must be stated up front: e.g. a vLLM-vs-llama.cpp comparison at AWQ-4bit vs GGUF-Q4_K_M is not a clean precision match, and the writeup has to say so.

examples.name: output_sweep
examples.description: Hypothesis (embedded-ai-chain/docs/paper.md P3): generation budget dominates the perception budget - increasing max_tokens raises latency and energy substantially more than a comparable change to input length. Varied: output_tokens. Held constant: model, backend, platform, input length, batch, concurrency, sampling, power mode. Expected to move: e2e latency, decode time, energy per request. Expected NOT to move: TTFT, prefill throughput.
